questions.question: State the general formula for alkanes and give an example of a straight‑chain alkane with five carbon atoms.
Explain why the boiling point of n‑hexane is higher than that of n‑butane.
Calculate the number of moles of propane in 44.1 g of the gas.
Describe the mechanism of the free‑radical halogenation of methane to produce chloromethane.
State the product of the reaction between 1‑bromopropane and sodium ethoxide in ethanol.
Compare the reactivity of 1‑chlorobutane and 2‑chlorobutane towards nucleophilic substitution by sodium hydroxide in aqueous solution.

A student performs the following experiment: 10.0 g of 1‑bromopropane is reacted with excess sodium ethoxide in ethanol. The product is isolated and found to be 7.5 g of propene. Calculate the percent yield of the reaction.
Explain why alkenes undergo addition reactions rather than substitution reactions.
Describe the stereochemistry of the product formed when propene reacts with bromine in an anti‑addition manner.
Evaluate the environmental impact of using ethylene as a feedstock for the production of polyethylene compared with using propylene.
